explanation: "Which finite groups have the smallest biggest product-free sets?" is formalized as determining the supremum α of exponents for which every nontrivial finite group of order n has a product-free set of size ≥ c·n^α. This is a reasonable quantitative proxy for Green's open-ended question, matching his discussion of whether Kedlaya's 11/14 is sharp. Excluding the trivial group is correct. The statement is a faithful interpretation.
